version.changelog:
- Removes the Distil-Whisper-Large-v3 automatic speech recognition (ASR) backend; now lists 6 ASR models instead of 7.
- Updates documentation to reflect the new set of supported ASR models.
- Keeps all other functionality, features, and usage the same.

llm.summary: This is a coherent self-hosted speech transcription and text-to-speech skill, with sensitive audio and voice-cloning risks that users should manage deliberately.

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities match the stated purpose: ASR, TTS, URL-based audio fetching, staged files, MCP access, and optional Qwen3 voice cloning from user-provided clips. Voice cloning and audio handling are sensitive, but they are disclosed and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to a user-configured talkies server and use ordinary curl, Docker, and MCP workflows. The file staging API can list, read, upload, and delete staged audio, so access should be limited to trusted clients.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is documented as running a Docker container and mounting a data directory; no hidden installer, obfuscated command, or unrelated package activity appears in the skill artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The service may bind on port 8000 and default to no auth unless TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN is set. The documentation discloses this and recommends auth, loopback binding, reverse proxy controls, and private-download blocking for exposed deployments.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Model weights, staged uploads, URL-download cache, and custom voice clips persist under the mounted data directory until deleted. This is disclosed and proportionate to the service, with no unexplained privilege escalation or hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you run or trust the talkies server. Set TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN, bind to localhost or put the service behind TLS and access controls if exposed, and enable TALKIES_BLOCK_PRIVATE_DOWNLOADS for untrusted clients. Treat uploaded audio, cached URL downloads, transcripts, and custom voice clips as sensitive data; delete staged files and custom voices when no longer needed. Use voice cloning only with clear permission from the speaker and in compliance with applicable law and policy.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The URL file_path and server-side cache behavior is expected for this service and is documented, including file listing, deletion, size caps, and an SSRF-blocking option. The first quick-start example could more prominently warn that URLs and downloaded audio are handled and retained by the talkies server.
[SQP-2] expected: Voice cloning from reference clips is an advertised, user-directed feature. The scanner concern is valid as user guidance because the docs lack an explicit consent and biometric-data warning, but the behavior is not hidden or purpose-mismatched.
[SQP-2] expected: The setup guide gives operational voice-cloning steps with local custom voice files. This is coherent with the TTS purpose, but users should add consent, access-control, and retention practices around those clips.
